correctness.rationale: Partition ordered edge pairs by matching/different directions, each edge of uniform weight 1/(d 2^{d−1}). Different directions: mismatched other fixed bits K~Bin(d−2,1/2), and independent endpoint offsets U,V~Unif(0,1), D=K+U+V. Same direction: mismatched fixed bits K~Bin(d−1,1/2), K=0 gives |S−T| density ℓ; K≥1 gives K+min(S+T,2−S−T) with density h=2t on (0,1). Assemble mixture with kernel g(t)=min(t,2−t) on (0,2). Only h kernels jump at integer endpoints, with exact displayed magnitudes; ℓ and g are continuous there as asserted. Exact mixture integrations reproduce mass, mean and second moment; independent four-endpoint shortest-path evaluations for d3..5 and rational edge coordinates yielded 22,704 matches, with broader 22,829 bounded checks. Coupling to different-direction event with failure 1/d and binomial Berry–Esseen proves the uniform O(d^{-1/2}) CLT. Bounded comparisons do not establish all d.

value.rationale: The complete probability law of intrinsic distances between uniformly sampled points on a classical d-cube wireframe is a natural geometric invariant. The nontrivial all-dimensional binomial jump spectrum, exact moments, and normal limit distinguish it from a simple mean calculation; exact formulas can be reused in graph-metric probability and benchmarking.
residual_risks: The earlier mean-distance identity could be known, and a previously unlocated shape-distance law may cover the exact distribution.

final_claim: For independent arclength-uniform points on the intrinsic unit-edge metric graph Q_d, d≥3, an exact mixture of same-edge triangular, parallel-edge folded-triangular, and different-direction two-uniform kernels gives the complete distribution. At k=2..d−1, f_d(k−)−f_d(k+)=2 binom(d−1,k−1)/(d2^{d−1}); exact first and second moments and a Berry–Esseen O(d^{-1/2}) central limit law follow.
